Add Custom Titles and Axis Labels to a Plotly Figure

Source: R/ro_ply_title.R
ro_ply_title.Rd

This function adds a (custom styled) main title, y-axis label, and/or x-axis label as annotations to a Plotly figure, using RIVM theming and Dutch number formatting. It automatically calculates left margin spacing based on the longest y-axis label.

Usage

ro_ply_title(
  fig,
  y_data = NULL,
  y_label = NULL,
  x_label = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  base_family = "RijksoverheidSansWebText",
  canvas_width = 776,
  left_margin_base = 10,
  char_width = 7,
  title_size = 17,
  axis_title_size = 13,
  title_color = ro_color(color_name = "lintblauw"),
  thousand_seperator = ".",
  decimal_seperator = ","
)

Arguments

fig

A plotly figure object created by plotly::plot_ly() to which the titles and labels will be added.

y_data

Used to determine the longest y-axis label for margin calculation.

y_label

Y-axis label to display.

x_label

X-axis label to display.

title

Main title to display at the top left.

base_family

Font family to use.

canvas_width

Width of the plotting area in pixels.

left_margin_base

Base left margin in pixels.

char_width

Estimated width per character in pixels.

title_size

Font size for the main title.

axis_title_size

Font size for axis titles.

title_color

Color for all titles/labels.

thousand_seperator

Separator for thousands in y-axis labels.

decimal_seperator

Separator for decimals in y-axis labels.

Value

The plotly figure object with added (and styled) title and/or axis labels as annotations.

See also

Other plotly: ro_ply_add_theme(), ro_ply_cursor(), ro_ply_dim(), ro_ply_disable_toolbar(), ro_ply_focus_linechart(), ro_ply_keyboard_nav_barchart(), ro_ply_keyboard_nav_bargraph(), ro_ply_keyboard_nav_legend(), ro_ply_keyboard_nav_linechart(), ro_ply_keyboard_nav_trendline(), ro_ply_legend_theme(), ro_ply_theme()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Title only:
ro_ply_title(fig,  y_data = data$'Number of Cases', title = "Fancy title")
# Y-axis label only:
ro_ply_title(fig, y_label = "Number of cases")
# X-axis label only:
ro_ply_title(fig, x_label = "Groups")
# Title, Y-axis label, and X-axis label in one go:
ro_ply_title(fig, y_data = data$'Number of Cases',
  y_label = "Number of cases", title = "Fancy title", x_label = "groups")
} # }
